text:
The water of the sky mingling with the water of the sea.
Swimming through them in the boat advancing in silence,
with ecstatic estrangement, frantic insistence
that it never end, that it always remain there,
with me, clasping me in vertiginous rite,
the two twin waters, the two identical waters,
the two eternal pure waters in which the moon
magically disintegrated.

And today, radiant, unique day of September,
joy of the two blue seas, one and two in the same,
shores of La Manga, burning with earth!
which hold and separate them, divide and join them
in the endless double Junction, the key
to this sea, so intimate and complex.

Today, yes, my two seas in their double contact,
in alternating, unison surrender of force,
the two seas loved as one, the one they are,
the immense sea that is sky for every water,
with sun and moon, wind and catch;
with this volcanic rhythm of buried ardor
in sweet, almost mystical geology.

Night and morning of the sea, round dense day
of sun and phantoms slipping through blue light
of a long voyage in a boat that falls silent
so I can hear, mine, hard and compact,
the terrible pulse, delicately full,
of a sun-sea, a moon-sea;
of dreaming or remembering oneself in sleep,
of living or burning in the light…

You, always you, stranger and ours at every hour,
clean and fragrant, scented and light, strong and populated,
an entire universe inside the lantern without escape
that is this land’s voracious embrace!

translation.title: The Water of the Sky Mingling with the Water of the Sea…
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. ‘La Manga’ and the poem’s sea/sky doubling are retained.
